citation.title: EU Accused of Inviting Fossil Fuel Executives to COP28 Under False Pretences

question: Whether the European Commission gave Party Overflow badges to five fossil fuel company representatives for COP28 on the stated grounds that they were panellists at EU side events, and whether that explanation holds.
data: Not stated as a dataset. The article rests on a letter from the EU Climate Commissioner to MEPs (described, not reproduced), the Commission's answers to the outlet's questions, a statement from Eni, quotes from campaigners and MEPs, and a figure of 2,456 fossil fuel lobbyists at COP28 that is linked to a third-party newsletter (heated.world). The page does not say which participant list or classification produced the 2,456 figure.
method: Journalistic: questioned the Commission and companies about whether named invitees took part in EU side events (intro, paragraphs 6-8, 20). No method is given for identifying or counting fossil fuel lobbyists.

definitions.definition: Not defined. The page uses the term as the badge type the EU says the five company representatives received.
definitions.quote: received a Party Overflow badge on the grounds that they were panellists in specific side-events

definitions.term: EU delegation (who counts as part of it)
definitions.definition: Not defined in general. The Commission's spokesperson states that the badge holders were not considered part of the EU delegation and had no access to its offices.
definitions.quote: do not have access to our delegation offices nor would they be considered as part of the EU delegation.

definitions.definition: Not defined. The term is used for people from oil and gas companies and is not tied to a stated classification.
definitions.quote: At least 2,456 fossil fuel lobbyists were granted access to the Dubai summit

proxies.indicator: Employment by named oil and gas companies (BP, ExxonMobil, Eni); for the wider count, a figure taken from a linked third-party newsletter with no stated indicator.
proxies.quote: The EU invited five representatives of fossil fuel giants, including executives from BP, ExxonMobil, and Eni

findings.claim: The Commission says the five company representatives got a Party Overflow badge because they were panellists at specific side events.
findings.quote: received a Party Overflow badge on the grounds that they were panellists in specific side-events

findings.claim: According to the outlet, two of the five did not take part in any EU events, which it says casts doubt on the Commission's explanation.
findings.quote: two of the executives did not in fact participate in any EU events at COP28

findings.claim: The Commission admitted, when asked, that the two invitees did not take part in events; the outlet says the claimed last-minute replacements were more junior staff.
findings.quote: the European Commission admitted that neither took part in events, when questioned by DeSmog

findings.claim: A company confirmed that its invited executive did not speak at any COP28 event.
findings.quote: didn’t speak at any events at COP28

findings.claim: The Commission says the badge holders were outside the EU delegation. This is the Commission's position, not an independent check.
findings.quote: do not have access to our delegation offices nor would they be considered as part of the EU delegation.

findings.claim: Badge holders could attend open side events but not the formal negotiations.
findings.quote: though they could not access the formal negotiations.

findings.claim: A figure of at least 2,456 fossil fuel lobbyists at COP28 is reported, said to be nearly four times any previous year. The article attributes it only by a hyperlink to heated.world.
findings.quote: At least 2,456 fossil fuel lobbyists were granted access to the Dubai summit – nearly four times more than any previous year.

limitations.point: The text read is the full saved web page (about 1,110 words, 32 paragraphs), but it is a news article and not a study. It does not describe how badge types work, how organisations are classified, or how the 2,456 figure was counted.

The 2,456 figure is secondhand: the page only links it to heated.world. Its underlying data (for example the UNFCCC participant list) and classification rules are not stated here and must be checked at that source before use.

The Commission's letter is quoted only in part; the article does not reproduce it or give the full list of five invitees' badge details. Whether a Party Overflow badge counts as being in a delegation is stated only as the Commission's view.
The outlet is a campaigning and investigative news site and the article quotes advocates and politicians critical of the Commission. Treat the claims as reported, not verified. Exxon did not respond.
limitations.quote: Exxon didn’t respond to DeSmog’s request for comment.

limitations.point: The saved text contains no instructions addressed to a reader or an AI (only 'Subscribe' and 'Donate' page furniture).
